A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ROSE, with the same authors, core components and experimental program despite the changed title. The main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original ROSE forecasting results, ablations, efficiency measurements and appendix experiments, including short-term forecasting on M4.

after.justification: v3 retains original forecasting, ablation, efficiency and supplementary experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Both retain multi-frequency masking and reconstruction, the clustered TS-Register, Top-K transfer, low-rank token adjustment and joint training losses. v3 omits the RevIN description, but does not establish that normalization was removed from the procedure.

E1.justification: The pre-training collection, seven long-term forecasting benchmarks, M4 evaluation and cross-domain and rare-pattern scenarios are retained. The pre-training and evaluation dataset tables exchange numbers, without changing coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across full-shot, few-shot, zero-shot, M4 and supplementary comparisons. S2P-LLM/S2IP-LLM label corrections identify the same comparator; the added explanation of MOMENT documents an existing comparison.

E3.justification: The stated splits, 512-step inputs, forecast horizons, training-data fractions and efficiency-test batch size remain unchanged. v3 newly discloses drop_last=False and MOMENT's evaluation procedure, without establishing revisions to earlier settings. MAE remains reported in Appendix Table 15 despite its removal from the summary table.

E4.justification: The component and masking ablations, alternative pre-training tasks, scalability and sensitivity studies, architecture-generality tests and forecasting case studies are retained. Added t-SNE implementation details explain the existing Figure 1 analysis rather than introduce a new analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix A.8 retains three runs with different random seeds, standard-deviation reporting, the PatchTST comparison and Table 11's 99% confidence-interval column. The reported uncertainty values also match.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes Chronos's Traffic MSE from 0.371 to 0.615, matching Table 15 already present in v2. Table 8 and Figure 5 change TimesFM's reported runtime from 167.2 to 10.5 seconds and MOMENT's from 88 to 13 seconds. The detailed forecasting and ablation result tables otherwise match numerically.

T1.justification: v3 removes Section 3's explicit mathematical problem definition, including multivariate input/target notation and the pairwise-disjoint pre-training, fine-tuning and test-set assumption. The method equations (1)–(12) remain substantively unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain unified representation learning through frequency decomposition and adaptive transfer through TS-Register. The claims of lightweight forecasting, strong full-shot performance and competitive few-shot and zero-shot capabilities are retained despite abstract and title revisions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1.4 newly qualifies the MOMENT comparison: its masked-reconstruction forecasting adaptation is not an officially supported zero-shot use. Section 4 also explicitly emphasizes ROSE's long-term forecasting focus. Existing mechanism explanations and interpretations otherwise remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds drop_last=False, encoder-output t-SNE details and MOMENT's masked-reconstruction evaluation procedure. It replaces the anonymous ROSE code link with a named GitHub repository, but removes the RevIN description and standardized evaluation-data download link. Most hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds forecasting, domain-modeling and benchmarking references, including DUET, CATCH and TSFM-Bench. It removes the LLM-focused related-work paragraph and Time-LLM/TEMPO references, alongside the RevIN and dataset-survey citations. The central positioning around unified representations and adaptive transfer remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, edits the abstract and selected introduction/architecture passages, removes standalone problem-definition and reproducibility material, and adds impact, acknowledgement and appendix explanations. Most prose and section organization remain intact. Tables 12–14 introduce inconsistent ReadyTS labels for the retained ROSE results.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column layout to an ICML two-column layout, with extensive resizing and repositioning of figures and tables and appendix reflow. Table 2 becomes MSE-only, Tables 5–6 exchange order, and Figure 5 repositions the revised runtime points. Existing experimental displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting the Chronos–Traffic summary inconsistency and explaining MOMENT's nonstandard forecasting use improve accuracy and interpretation. Added evaluation and t-SNE details provide further modest transparency gains. These benefits are partly offset by removing RevIN and standardized-data instructions and introducing inconsistent ReadyTS labels. The net improvement is limited, with essentially unchanged methods and experimental evidence.
